Alex: quick check — CI is failing a contract test for /v1/completions around how 'stop' is handled. noticed the python sdk sends stop=None -> JSON null, while TS omits the key. @Maria @Jayden can you take a look?
Maria: I dug in — py-sdk serializes stop=None as "stop": null, TS omits the key. Server lately treats null differently (it ends up being interpreted as an explicit empty stop list which changes KV cache hits).
Jayden: hmm, server used to treat null as missing but after the routing/perf change the strict schema path treats null != missing. that's the regression vector. we can either accept null==missing server-side or normalize in SDKs.
Priya: quick preference: changing server semantics is higher risk. prefer SDK normalization so clients send the canonical minimal payload (omit None).
Alex: agreed. Maria — think you can ship a small py-sdk change to drop None keys in the request body? where would that live?
Maria: yep — working on a tiny PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/pull/828. Patch uses simple filter in request builder to skip None values and adds a unit test. example change:
```py
# before
body = {"prompt": prompt, "stop": stop}
# after
body = {k: v for k, v in body.items() if v is not None}
```
added a test that asserts the outgoing JSON has no 'stop' key when stop is None.
Jayden: thanks. note: analytics/telemetry code sometimes expects explicit keys, so ensure any metrics shim falls back if key missing. also confirm TS codegen actually omits undefined vs sending null. @Maria can you add an integration test hitting sandbox so we catch regressions in e2e? ci-bot flagged this in contract-suite.
ci-bot: Contract suite job #5727 failed on main at 1769001200 — mismatch null vs missing for 'stop' field. job: https://ci/redwood/5727
Maria: will add integration test and a changelog note. PR will target a patch release branch.
Priya: also let's update the API docs sentence to say explicitly: "omit optional params to use server defaults; null is not guaranteed to be treated as missing." that should reduce ambiguity.
Alex: sgtm. Jayden — could you add a short defensive server shim that treats null == missing for now so existing clients don't break prior to patch rollouts? maybe log a warning when we see null for optional fields.
Jayden: yep, I can open a small PR to server/main to normalize null->omit and emit a warning log key 'null_stop_received'. will add e2e to ensure no behavioral change for explicit empty lists.
deploy-bot: canary deployed service/completions at sha abc123 — watch for logs containing 'null_stop_received'.
Alex: thanks all. I'll ping docs & SDK owners when both PRs merge. leaving thread open until both merges are green. :eyes:
